authority.offset_convention: Zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets into the frozen authority; end_byte_exclusive is half-open.

allocation.rule: Stable IDs are assigned in ascending order of each accepted unit's earliest frozen-source locus; producer IDs are preserved separately.

preconditions: The input must have exactly the authority byte count and SHA-256 above.
Each old_text UTF-8 byte sequence must equal the authority bytes at its stated half-open interval.
Each old_text must have the stated occurrence_count_in_frozen_authority in the complete frozen file.
All operation intervals must be pairwise nonoverlapping.
application_contract.application_order: Apply operations in descending start_byte order so frozen-source offsets remain valid.

units.proof_rationale: The basis member is chosen after and for each point x, so it depends on x rather than only on the possibly repeated cover index i_x. Indexing the refinement by U binds every chosen B_x and proves the stated refinement.
units.adverse_evidence: With the one-member cover U_0=R and a basis of bounded rational intervals, every i_x is 0 but no single basis interval B_0 covers R; the printed J={i_x} construction therefore fails.

operations.old_text:
If $ x \in U = \bigcup_{i\in I} U_i $, there is an $ i_x \in I $ such that
$ x \in U_{i_x} $. Thus we have a $ B_{i_x} \in \mathcal{B}$
verifying $ x \in B_{i_x} \subset U_{i_x}$. Set
$J = \{i_x | x \in U\}$ and for $j = i_x \in J$ set $V_j = B_{i_x}$.
This gives the desired open covering of $U$ by $\{V_j\}_{j \in J}$.
operations.replacement_text:
For every $x \in U = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$, choose $i_x \in I$ and
$B_x \in \mathcal{B}$ such that $x \in B_x \subset U_{i_x}$.
Set $J = U$ and, for $j = x \in J$, set $V_j = B_x$.
This gives the desired open covering of $U$ by $\{V_j\}_{j \in J}$.

units.proof_rationale: For f:X to Y, inverse image accepts subsets of Y and returns subsets of X. The complement law is f^{-1}(Y\E)=X\f^{-1}(E) for E subset Y.
units.adverse_evidence: The printed identity puts X inside f^{-1}, puts Y on the result side, and quantifies E as a subset of X, reversing all three required types.

operations.old_text:

operations.replacement_text:
Finally, (2) and (3) equivalence follows from $f^{-1}(Y \setminus E) = X
\setminus f^{-1}(E)$ for all subsets $E \subset Y$.

units.proof_rationale: DCC supplies a minimal member under inclusion, and the contradiction proof uses only the absence of a strictly smaller member of A.
units.adverse_evidence: A finite DCC poset can have incomparable minimal elements and no least element, so 'smallest' is not implied.

units.adverse_evidence: The printed ellipsis followed by Z_n is juxtaposition, not the finite set union used by the proof.

units.proof_rationale: Distributivity expands G_m intersected with the finite union X_1 union ... union X_n as the finite union of every G_m intersect X_i.
units.adverse_evidence: Without the final union operator the right side concatenates the ellipsis and last term and does not state the equality used for stabilization.

units.proof_rationale: The replacement eliminates the selected bad tuple without creating a new one, so N strictly decreases; it can eliminate additional tuples simultaneously, hence termination is after at most the original N repetitions.
units.adverse_evidence: A finite discrete example with two bad tuples sharing the refined first entry makes N fall from 2 to 0 in one replacement, disproving 'decreased by one'.

operations.old_text:
A simple check shows that $N$ has decreased by one under this replacement.
Repeating this procedure $N$ times we arrive at the situation where
$N = 0$.
operations.replacement_text:
A simple check shows that $N$ has decreased by at least one under this
replacement. Repeating this procedure at most the original $N$ times,
we arrive at the situation where $N = 0$.

units.proof_rationale: Noetherian DCC supplies a minimal closed member of the counterexample family, and the proof uses only that every proper closed subset is outside that family.
units.adverse_evidence: DCC does not imply that a nonempty family has a least member, so 'smallest' overstates the available order-theoretic conclusion.

units.proof_rationale: Finite unions of point closures are closed, contained in T, directed by inclusion through union of finite index sets, and have union T. This proves the stated directed-union characterization.
units.adverse_evidence: In a two-point discrete space the family of the two point closures has no member containing their union, so the family exhibited by the printed proof need not be directed.
